h1: The 6 Best Jar Openers for One-Handed Use of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Jar Openers for One-Handed Use: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 jar openers for one-handed use compared on mounting, teeth design, lid range, materials and power needs.
summary: The Jar Jaw Under-Cabinet opener is the best choice for most one-handed cooks, gripping lids with a rubber V that will not scar the metal. The Moeuonb stainless model is the sturdy pick for vacuum-sealed lids, the Delfori bites hardest with two rows of teeth, and the EMSON Robotwist is the only one that turns the lid for you.
intro: One-handed jar opening is a leverage problem, not a strength problem. A standard gripper wants one hand on the jar and the other on the tool. An under-cabinet opener fixes that by holding the lid still while the jar does the turning, so the one working hand only has to rotate the glass. The catch is that every one of these needs a place to mount.

We ranked six openers from the listings: mounting style, grip surface, tooth design, lid range, materials and whether the design uses power. Three mounts to the underside of a cabinet with screws, one is an adaptive handheld, and one is an automatic motorized model. Rental kitchens rule out drilling, so we note where a pick avoids it.

products.name: Jar Jaw Under-Cabinet Jar Opener
products.verdict: A rubber V-grip under-cabinet opener with no sharp metal teeth, which also closes jars.
products.description:
The Jar Jaw mounts under a cabinet and grips lids with a rubber V-grip, using no sharp metal teeth. It also works as a jar closer.

It ranks first because a rubber grip protects the lid, which matters for jars you keep using, and the V shape adjusts to many diameters. It trails the metal-toothed openers on grip on very tight vacuum lids. That is the cost of the gentle surface.

Buy it if you want a gentle opener that will not mark lids. Skip it if tight, factory-sealed lids are the main problem. It suits a home where drilling into a cabinet is allowed.
pros: Rubber grip will not scar lids
cons: Less bite on tight vacuum seals
products.idealFor: One-handed users who want a gentle grip.

products.name: Moeuonb Under-Cabinet Stainless Jar Opener
products.verdict: An all-stainless under-cabinet opener with hardened teeth for factory-sealed lids.
products.description:
The Moeuonb is all stainless steel, has hardened wear-resistant teeth, mounts under a cabinet and is made for vacuum-sealed lids.

It ranks second because metal teeth bite where rubber slips, and the stainless body is the sturdiest build here. It sits behind the Jar Jaw because the teeth mark lids. The Delfori adds a second row of teeth for more bite.

Buy it if tough factory-sealed lids are the main trouble. Skip it if you want to protect the lids. Its stainless body will outlast most plastic rivals.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want a permanent opener for factory-sealed lids.

products.name: Delfori Under-Cabinet Jar Opener
products.verdict: Two rows of high-carbon steel teeth, with a range from large jars to spice bottles.
products.description:
The Delfori mounts under a cabinet, has two rows of high-carbon steel teeth and fits jars from big ones down to spice bottles.

It ranks third because two rows of teeth give the firmest hold in the group. It loses to the Moeuonb on listing detail about the stainless build and hardened teeth, and the teeth are sharp, which matters if you rest a hand near them.

Buy it if you want the strongest bite and the lid size varies. Skip it if sharp edges worry you. Keep a hand clear when the jar slips free.
pros: Fits spice bottles to big jars
products.idealFor: Cooks who want the firmest bite.

products.name: EZ Off Under-Cabinet Jar Opener
products.verdict: A straightforward under-cabinet opener made for one-handed use that saves counter space.
products.description:
The EZ Off is an under-cabinet design made for one-handed use, with an easy-grip operation that takes no counter space.

It ranks fourth because it does the job simply, but the listing gives no detail on teeth or materials. It beats countertop gadgets on space and trails the named-material models on grip.

Buy it if you want a plain opener under the cabinet. Skip it if you want teeth or grip material specified. Check the cabinet depth before you buy.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a plain under-cabinet opener.
products.skipIf: You want specified teeth or materials.

products.name: Honeydak One-Handed Jar and Bottle Opener
products.verdict: A plastic and rubber one-handed opener for jars and bottles that needs no mounting.
products.description:
The Honeydak is a plastic body with a rubber interior that opens jars and bottles. You insert the lid and turn, and no drilling is needed.

It ranks fifth because it asks a bit more of the hand, since you still turn the tool, but it suits renters and travelers. At $25-50 it costs more than the under-cabinet models.

Buy it if you rent or travel. Skip it if you have a cabinet to mount to. It is also handy as a camping or travel tool.
cons: Still needs a turn from the hand
products.skipIf: You can mount to a cabinet.

products.name: EMSON Robotwist Deluxe Automatic Jar Opener
products.verdict: A fully automatic Deluxe model with self-adjusting vice grips for lids from 1.2 to 3.5 inches.
products.description:
The EMSON Robotwist Deluxe 7321 is fully automatic and hands-free, with higher torque and self-adjusting vice grips for lids from 1.2 to 3.5 inches.

It ranks last because it needs power and counter space and it is the bulkiest option here. It is the only one that turns the lid for you.

Buy it if you cannot twist at all. Skip it if you want a simple tool. It is the right call when pain rules out twisting entirely.
products.idealFor: People who cannot twist at all.

whatMatters.detail: An under-cabinet opener holds the lid still while the jar turns. That is what makes it one-handed. It needs screws and a cabinet with room beneath it. Check the listing for mounting hardware, and measure the gap below your cabinet. Measure the gap before you buy, because a tall pasta sauce jar needs more clearance than a pickle jar.

Rubber grips protect lids but slip on tight seals, while steel teeth bite hard but mark the lid. Two rows of teeth bite more. Look for the grip type on the listing, and choose by how often you open vacuum-sealed jars. A very tight seal is where rubber loses to steel, so match the grip to your toughest jars.

Openers cover a range of lid diameters, with the Robotwist listing 1.2 to 3.5 inches. A V-shaped grip adjusts widely. Check the listed range, and match it to your smallest spice jar and your biggest pickle jar. Spice jars are the usual trouble spot, since a narrow lid can slip out of a wide V.

All stainless or high-carbon steel resists wear, while plastic is lighter. Check the body material on the listing, and look for hardened teeth if you plan to use it for years. Hardened teeth matter if you use the opener daily, because soft teeth dull in a season.

A manual opener asks for a twist of the jar, and an automatic one turns the lid for you but needs power and space. Check the power source on the listing, and decide whether a twist is possible. If your hand cannot manage even a gentle turn, only an automatic model will solve it.

faq.a: The Moeuonb and Delfori use steel teeth that can mark lids, while the Jar Jaw uses rubber. The Honeydak uses a rubber interior. Choose by how much you value the lid. Matching the grip to the jar saves lids.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying a handheld gripper when you have one hand. Under-cabinet models like the Jar Jaw hold the lid for you so the working hand only turns the jar. Tall jars need clearance below the unit.

faq.q: Is the EMSON worth it over a mounted opener?
faq.a: If you cannot twist at all, yes. The EMSON Robotwist turns the lid with a motor for lids 1.2 to 3.5 inches, but a mounted opener is simpler and cheaper. Check the lid range against your smallest and largest jar.
Mark the cabinet underside, drill pilot holes and screw the bracket in with the jar's height in mind. Check the gap so a tall jar can turn. Use the right screws for the cabinet material.

faq.q: How do I look after one?
faq.a: Wipe the grip after sticky jars and brush out lid fragments from the teeth. Rubber like the Jar Jaw's lasts longer when kept clean. Dry it after sticky jars to prevent rust.
The Honeydak opens jars and bottles, and the Delfori fits spice bottles. Other models focus on jar lids. Check the range on the listing first.

finalTake: The Jar Jaw Under-Cabinet Jar Opener is the best buy for most one-handed cooks, with a gentle rubber grip. The Moeuonb is better for tough vacuum seals, the Honeydak suits renters, and the EMSON Robotwist suits anyone who cannot twist. Check you have room under the cabinet before ordering.
